curation.notes: Custom single-beam optical tweezers pull membrane tethers with ConA-coated beads from NIH 3T3 fibroblasts and Xenopus retinal ganglion neurons cultured on glass or polyacrylamide gels of different stiffness, reporting peak and steady-state tether forces (with/without blebbistatin). Traction force microscopy is a separate complementary assay; the 532 nm wavelength in the auto record belongs to a notch dichroic, not the trapping laser.

evidence.snippet: a 5-W 1064-nm ytterbium fibre laser (YLM-5-LP, IPG Laser, Germany) was used at a high power (>1 W) to minimize intensity fluctuations.
Excess power was redirected to a beam dump and the power at the optical trap itself was 600 mW.
Beads of one size (2.16 µm) were used, ConA coated beads were prepared freshly for each experiment under temperature-controlled conditions
Beads were then moved away from the cell at 0.1 µm/s in the case of 3T3 fibroblasts and 0.5 µm/s in the case of neurons, leading to the formation of a membrane tether between the cell and the bead.
we probed the effective membrane tension of neurons and fibroblasts cultured on glass and polyacrylamide substrates of varying stiffness using optical tweezers.
